effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (the Silver Dragon Value Box reprint of DPKB-EN023)

transitions.historical_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" from your Deck. There can only be 1 face-up "Malefic" monster on the field. Other monsters you control cannot declare an attack. If there is no face-up Field Spell Card on the field, destroy this card.
transitions.modern_text: Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set. Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by banishing 1 "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" from your Deck. There can only be 1 "Malefic" monster on the field. Other monsters you control cannot declare an attack. If there is no face-up Field Spell Card on the field, destroy this card.
transitions.summary: Wording only for the summoning restriction, on Konami's period rulings (round 035). The era text "This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 \"Blue-Eyes White Dragon\" from your Deck" is the wording Konami's strategy article (printed 2009-12-07) says can be revived after one proper Summon, Konami's rulebook (Versions 7.0 to 8.0) says the same of any properly Summoned Special Summon Monster, and Konami's Extreme Victory rulings (compiled 2011-05-12) say it of Meklord Astro Dragon Asterisk, whose text uses the same "can only be Special Summoned by" wording. So the era card and the errata'd "Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by banishing 1 \"Blue-Eyes White Dragon\" from your Deck" revive alike. The same printing also drops "face-up" from "There can only be 1 face-up \"Malefic\" monster on the field"; that change is near-inert (a Malefic monster cannot be Set) and no source read rules on it. No behavioural difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

implementation_metadata.reason: Round 035: the generated card 600000008 (rounds 029 and 031) was removed and its number retired. On Konami's period rulings the modern card behaves as the era card did at the snapshots this record applies at, so the modern implementation is used; no script or engine test is needed for it.

review.notes:
upstream_implementations contains only 513000068 "Malefic Blue-Eyes White Dragon (Anime)" in cards-unofficial.cdb, which is a DIFFERENT card - it sends "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" from Deck to the Graveyard as its Summon cost, keys its self-destruction to "Malefic World" (Duel.IsEnvironment(27564031)) rather than any Field Spell, and has no attack-lock on your other monsters; text ratio 0.6517. It is not a historical implementation of 9433350 and cannot be a baseline, so this card remains a genuine gap. Era text: DPKB-EN023 released 2010-04-16 (EU/OCE) and 2010-04-20 (NA), days before the 2010-04-24 Edison snapshot, so v0 is the Edison text; the card postdates GOAT entirely. Trailing cosmetic revision v1 -> v2 (LDS2-EN005, 2021-01-21: "Field Spell Card" -> "Field Spell") is not recorded as a change; cards.cdb matches v2 exactly. The dropped "face-up" is near-inert in practice, since a Malefic monster cannot be Set, and is recorded only as part of the same printing's erratum. Malefic Blue-Eyes does not appear on the EdisonFormat.com Functional Errata list.

Round 035 (2026-09-29) correction. The strict-nomi call was read from the printed wording alone (this record's own review says so) and no period ruling was cited for it. Konami's rulebook, Versions 7.0 (capture 2008-12-30), 7.1 (2010-03-30), 7.2 (2011-05-16) and 8.0 (linked from Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18), says of Special Summon Monsters: "You cannot use a card effect to Special Summon those monsters from your hand, Deck, or the Graveyard unless it was properly Special Summoned first." Konami's TCG strategy article (printed date 2009-12-07; earliest capture 2015-11-06) says a monster worded "This card can only be Special Summoned by..." can be Special Summoned again from the Graveyard after one proper Summon, and reserves the permanent lock for "cannot be Special Summoned except by...". This card's text says "can only be", so the era card and the errata'd card revive alike. Evidence and its limits: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, sections 3 and 6. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: the era text is a strict nomi - "This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 \"Blue-Eyes White Dragon\" from your Deck" - naming no source zone and permitting no other Special Summon ever. The errata'd text is semi-nomi and zone-bound, "Must first be Special Summoned (from your hand) by banishing 1 \"Blue-Eyes White Dragon\" from your Deck", so the modern card may be revived by generic Special Summons once it has been properly Summoned. The same revision drops "face-up" from "There can only be 1 face-up \"Malefic\" monster on the field", widening the uniqueness Condition to any Malefic on the field regardless of position." Superseded implementation note, kept verbatim: "Round 031: implemented by a project-authored script under the custom-script strategy (data/custom-cards/c600000008.json; passcode 600000008). Previously recorded as a known gap with gap_reason "Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode" (gap_sources ignis-babelcdb, yugipedia-card-errata). Status is partial, not complete: the custom card's not_reproduced list names what the script does not establish." Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In an Edison snapshot EDOPro lets a Malefic Blue-Eyes that already hit the field be Special Summoned again from the Graveyard by Monster Reborn or Call of the Haunted, which the era's "can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 \"Blue-Eyes White Dragon\" from your Deck" text forbids."
